To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the distribution of collagenases and denatured collagen in aging and OA cartilage is similar to that of MMP-1 and MMP-13, and that the cleavage sites of collagenase are not restricted to the triple helix of the collagen molecule.

the sites of collagenase cleavages in the collagenous matrix of articular cartilage are not randomly distributed and that these sites correlate with the denatured collagen in aging and in osteoarthritic cartilage.
the distribution of collagenase (MMP-1) and collagenase-3 (MMP-13) in aging and oste- oarthritic articular tissues is similar and is not related to the distribution of collagen II cleavage products.

the molecular basis of the pathogenesis of osteoarthritis (OA), with a focus on the role of the matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs).
the molecular basis of osteoarthritis (OA), with the aim of developing new therapeutic approaches for the treatment of OA.
the molecular mechanisms of the aging process and age-associated diseases
